summary.headline: Jury throws out Musk's suit against OpenAI; power concentration rises
summary.body: The day's main story came from a courtroom in Oakland. A federal jury rejected all of Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI, Sam Altman and Microsoft as time-barred, clearing the way for OpenAI's IPO and for-profit structure. Separately, Anthropic bought Stainless, a startup that builds SDKs for other AI companies. Both stories push up Power Concentration: more of the AI stack sits with a few big players. That helps Enslaved God (a powerful AI held by one owner) and Benevolent Dictator, and hurts Libertarian Utopia, which needs power to stay spread out. A small counterweight came from Cursor shipping a cheaper coding model built on China's open-weight Kimi K2.5. Horizon Balance fell 0.33 to 1.6.
summary.movers_note: Libertarian Utopia -0.6 and Enslaved God +0.6, mostly from the Musk verdict (-0.48/+0.48) with the Stainless deal adding -0.18/+0.18; Benevolent Dictator +0.5 from the same two stories.

events.title: Jury rejects Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and Altman
events.summary: A federal jury in Oakland rejected all of Musk's claims against OpenAI, Sam Altman and Microsoft as time-barred, clearing a path for OpenAI's IPO and for-profit structure.
events.reason: Removes legal obstacle to OpenAI's consolidation and capital raising; verdict reported May 18 (NYT), some outlets say May 19.

events.title: Anthropic acquires SDK maker Stainless
events.summary: Anthropic bought Stainless, the startup that builds SDKs for the OpenAI API, Cloudflare and others.
events.reason: Small acqui-hire of developer tooling used by a rival.

events.title: Cursor releases Composer 2.5 coding model built on China's Kimi K2.5
events.summary: Cursor shipped Composer 2.5, built on Moonshot's open-weight Kimi K2.5, claiming parity with Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 on coding at lower cost.
events.reason: Open Chinese base model powering a top US coding product; diffusion away from closed labs. Self-reported benchmarks.
